overview: Against the Anglo-Dutch 1...f5, White plays 2.g4 as a gambit, wanting to open the g-file and the long diagonal after ...fxg4. Black can take and hold the pawn with ...Nf6 and ...e5, and White has a lead in development but weakened kingside. It is a risky, rarely played surprise.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Nc3, Bg2 and Qb3
Harass Black with Qb3 and Bg2 on the long diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Take on g4 and return the pawn if needed

typical_structures.structure: Dutch-like f-file with Black pawn on g4 and a loosened White kingside

character.notes: An early flank pawn sacrifice gives forcing but double-edged positions.

gambit.notes: After 2.g4 fxg4 Black has an extra pawn and can keep it.

soundness.notes: Considered dubious by most strong players.

structure.notes: The f-file and g-file open early.

character.reason: A wing pawn sacrifice gives double-edged tactical play.

gambit.reason: White plays 2.g4 and Black can keep the pawn after fxg4.

soundness.reason: Black can accept and play ...Nf6 with an extra pawn.

structure.reason: The f-file and g-file open while the centre is still undecided.

level.reason: Dubious so not Beginner; tactical lines.

plans.reason: White plays for time and attack against the loosened black king.
